summary: Turn infrastructure climate-risk evidence into adaptation appraisals, resilient specifications and lifecycle action plans. Explore the five-day course.
lede: Climate resilience in infrastructure projects involves using climate-risk evidence to guide asset design, investment and operations. For project managers, engineers and climate-risk specialists, the course develops skills to screen hazards, assess vulnerability and stress-test long-lived assets, then compare adaptation options and appraise costs and benefits. Participants also practise turning decisions into resilient specifications, action plans and monitoring measures across construction and operations.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for intermediate infrastructure professionals who assess climate exposure or embed adaptation choices in project preparation, delivery and asset operations.
modules: World Bank Screening and Hazard Evidence
prerequisites: Prior exposure to infrastructure project preparation, design, appraisal or asset operations is expected. Familiarity with climate hazards or initial climate-risk screening will help you apply the intermediate-level exercises. No coding or programming is required.
